acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Nash Castro donated his papers (and subsequent accruals) to the Rockefeller Archive Center as an "unrestriced gift" on March 9, 1992.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Nash Castro (1920-2018) was a long-time associate and environmental advisor to Laurance S. Rockefeller. Castro served with the National Park Service for thirty years, retiring as regional director of the National Capital Parks in 1969. As park service liaison to the White House in the 1960s, Castro was an advisor to Jacqueline Kennedy and Lady Bird Johnson. His association with LSR developed through their mutual involvement in Lady Bird Johnson's beautification projects, membership on her Committee for a More Beautiful National Capital, and participation in the White House Conference on Natural Beauty in 1965. In 1969 at LSR's urging, Castro joined the Palisades Interstate Park Commission and served as its executive director until 1990. The day after he retired from the PIPC, Castro went to work for LSR, serving as his environmental consultant from April 12, 1990, until LSR's death in 2004.

Castro advocated ardently for the award of a Congressional Gold Medal to LSR in 1990. As LSR's environmental consultant, he was particularly involved in the development of the Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park, various Hudson Valley projects, a biography project on LSR, as well as with visits and other activities with Lady Bird Johnson. Castro also served on the boards of Rockefeller-related organizations, including the American Conservation Association, Jackson Hole Preserve, Inc., Historic Hudson Valley, and the Woodstock Foundation.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Nash Castro papers reflect his work in the 1990s and early 2000s as conservation consultant to Laurance S. Rockefeller. A substantial portion of the papers pertains to Castro's efforts in 1989-1990 to secure a Congressional Gold Medal for LSR in recognition of his contributions in the areas of conservation and preservation. The collection highlights LSR's conservation activities and Castro's involvement in them, particularly in relation to the Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park, but also in the Hudson Valley, and Hawaii. Castro also facilitated, and sometimes helped host, visits and other interactions with Lady Bird Johnson. The collection also contains one or more interviews with LSR (including one on Lady Bird Johnson), and drafts of Robin Winks's biography of LSR.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Rockefeller Archive Center has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them, and has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection.
